indifferent

/in-DIF-er-uhnt/ - the stress falls on DIF · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indifferent means having no particular interest or concern.

Indifferent to the rain, the surveyor worked through the downpour without once glancing at the sky.

Worked Example

Offered the window or the aisle for the twelve-hour flight, Ravi told the agent to pick for him — and meant it. He was not being polite, and he was not paralyzed by the choice; the two seats simply weighed the same to him. His seatmate, who had paid extra for the window months ahead, found such indifference unimaginable.

Indifferent is exactly right because the choice makes no difference to him — the word's literal heart. It is cooler than apathetic, which condemns a person for lacking feeling they ought to have; being indifferent to seat assignments is harmless, even sensible.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unconcerned: Unconcerned means free of worry about an outcome — nothing about it is troubling you. Indifferent means free of preference: the options weigh the same, so none of them pulls you. A patient can be unconcerned about a routine test yet still hope it goes quickly; the indifferent patient would not care either way.

unmoved: Unmoved means an appeal was actually heard and nothing shifted — someone made the case, and it failed to change you. Indifferent needs no appeal at all: it is the standing absence of preference or concern before anyone argues. You are unmoved by something; you can be indifferent from the start.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

eager: leaning toward one outcome with appetite

attentive: giving full, active notice

Where it sits · how completely interest has switched off — lukewarm → indifferent → uncaring

lukewarm vs. indifferent: A lukewarm reader still holds a faint preference; the indifferent one has none at all.

uncaring vs. indifferent: Uncaring goes beyond indifferent and picks up blame: it is indifference exactly where concern was owed — a landlord uncaring about frozen pipes.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not

Root — differ

Root — differ: to set apart (Latin differre)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: in a state of

Put it together

Put it together: In- (not) + differ (to set apart) + -ent (in a state of) = in a state where nothing sets the options apart. If you are indifferent between two seats, literally no difference tips you either way — the word wears its logic on its sleeve.

Use the root in a new word: different

Use the root in a new word: different: The two proposals looked identical in cost but proved different in every detail that mattered.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Indifferent is the neutral member of this unit's not-caring family: it reports missing preference or concern without automatically condemning. Apathetic is the accusation — feeling itself has failed; nonchalant is only the surface — an appearance of unconcern that may be a performance. A judge should be indifferent between the parties; she should never be apathetic about the case.
